title: Prohibition on Contracting with Entities Using Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment
description: Implements the prohibition on contracting with entities that use Huawei, ZTE, or other designated telecommunications or video surveillance equipment. This clause is an enforcement mechanism for Section 889 of the FY19 NDAA.
intent: Prevent federal funding from supporting foreign technologies deemed a national security threat.
conditions: Applies to all federal contracts, including micro-purchases, with rare exceptions.
implementation_guidance: Ensure the contractor and any subcontractor do not use covered equipment or services. Conduct due diligence and maintain records. If discovered post-award, report to the contracting officer within one business day and provide a mitigation plan within ten.
assessment_method: Contractor representations, inspections, and audits.
metadata: {"penalties":"Contracts may be terminated, and contractors debarred or penalized for violations or failure to report covered technology usage.","reciprocity":"Direct enforcement of NDAA Section 889 prohibitions. Related to FAR 52.204-24.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
description: HIPAA sets national standards for the protection of health information. It applies to covered entities (health plans, providers, and clearinghouses) and their business associates handling Protected Health Information (PHI). The Security Rule and Privacy Rule define administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.
intent: Protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of PHI in electronic and paper formats.
conditions: Applies to any entity handling PHI, including government contractors providing health-related services.
implementation_guidance: Implement required safeguards per the HIPAA Security Rule. Conduct regular risk assessments, maintain privacy notices, and ensure breach notification processes. Train workforce members and document all policies and procedures.
assessment_method: HHS audits, internal risk assessments, and contractual privacy compliance checks.
metadata: {"penalties":"Violations may result in civil and criminal penalties, including fines up to $1.5M per violation category per year.","reciprocity":"Partially aligned with NIST frameworks (800-53, 800-66). Mapped to several CUI protection controls.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Guide for Mapping Types of Information and Information Systems to Security Categories
description: NIST SP 800-60 provides guidance for categorizing federal information and systems according to FIPS 199. It maps specific types of information (e.g., financial, privacy, legal) to security impact levels across confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
intent: Support accurate and standardized security categorization for system impact assessments.
conditions: Applies when performing security categorization for any federal system or federal data handled by a contractor.
implementation_guidance: Use the volume and appendices to determine the proper security impact levels for each data type handled by the system. Combine these values to derive the system's overall impact level (low/moderate/high).
assessment_method: Document review during RMF Step 1 or system authorization phase.
metadata: {"penalties":"Improper mappings can result in misclassification of risk and deployment of inappropriate security controls, leading to compliance failure.","reciprocity":"Supports FIPS 199 and feeds into RMF and NIST 800-37 process.","last_updated":"2025-01-01"}

title: Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
description: Cornerstone DoD clause for cybersecurity: requires contractors to provide "adequate security" for all Covered Defense Information (CDI) on their systems and to rapidly report any cyber incidents to DoD. "Covered defense information" includes Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and export-controlled or military-critical technical data. Specifically, contractors must implement NIST SP 800-171 controls on any internal information system that processes or stores CDI, and flow down the clause to subs. Contractors must report cyber incidents (within 72 hours typically) and preserve/log data for DoD review. They may also be required to submit malware samples and cooperate with DoD damage assessments. (This clause also references an optional DoD-provided incident collection system, DIBNet.)
intent: Ensure the protection of sensitive defense information and to provide visibility into cybersecurity incidents affecting DoD supply chains.
conditions: Applies to all DoD contractors handling CDI or operating contractor-owned systems storing, processing or transmitting CDI
implementation_guidance: Perform a gap assessment and fully implement NIST SP 800-171 security requirements on all covered contractor information systems (110 security controls covering access control, encryption, audit logs, incident response, etc.). Have an incident response plan and training so that any "cyber incident" (e.g. network breach) involving CDI is identified and reported to DoD within the required timeframe. Use DoD's online reporting portal to submit required incident details. Preserve forensic evidence (system images, log files) for 90 days as the clause mandates, and facilitate any DoD post-incident investigation or damage assessment. Flow this clause to all subcontracts handling CDI and ensure subs also implement 800-171 and report incidents.
assessment_method: Self-Assessment
metadata: {"penalties":"If a contractor fails to implement the required security controls or to report breaches, DoD can consider it a breach of contract, potentially resulting in termination for default or negative past performance ratings. DoD may also withhold award fees or exclude the contractor from future contracts. Not reporting an incident (or misrepresenting cybersecurity compliance) could invite False Claims Act liability. Additionally, a cyber incident not properly handled can lead to loss of sensitive DoD data – harming national security – which may bring intense scrutiny or suspension of the contractor.","reciprocity":"Shared/redundant compliance","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Security Requirements
description: This clause establishes baseline security requirements for contractors processing classified information. It mandates compliance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), and other DoD or agency-specific directives.
intent: Ensure classified information is safeguarded through standardized security procedures.
conditions: Applies when a contract involves access to classified information.
implementation_guidance: Contractors must maintain a facility clearance, appoint a Facility Security Officer (FSO), and implement controls in accordance with the NISPOM. Security violations must be reported to the appropriate authority, and subcontractors must comply with the same requirements.
assessment_method: Security inspections by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) or agency equivalent.
metadata: {"penalties":"Violations can lead to suspension or revocation of facility clearance, contract termination, or debarment.","reciprocity":"Aligns with government-wide industrial security protocols under the NISP.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems
description: Establishes security categories for federal information and information systems based on potential impact of a security breach.
intent: Provide a standardized approach for categorizing information and systems based on security impact.
conditions: Applies to all federal information systems.
implementation_guidance: Conduct a security categorization assessment based on potential impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
assessment_method: Security assessment and authorization process.
metadata: {"penalties":"Non-compliance may result in system authorization denial.","reciprocity":"Supports risk management framework.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Privacy or Security Safeguards
description: This clause mandates that contractors must not publish or disclose any sensitive information unless authorized, and that adequate safeguards must be applied to protect records subject to the Privacy Act or other sensitive data.
intent: Prevent unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of privacy-protected or sensitive government data.
conditions: Applies when a contract involves design, development, or operation of a system of records or sensitive information.
implementation_guidance: Implement technical, administrative, and physical controls to protect sensitive or Privacy Act data. Ensure access is limited to authorized personnel and provide training on handling restrictions.
assessment_method: Review of security plans and data handling procedures.
metadata: {"penalties":"Unauthorized disclosures can trigger Privacy Act violations, financial penalties, or civil liability.","reciprocity":"May overlap with NIST 800-53 privacy controls and agency-specific privacy programs.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
description: NIST SP 800-53 provides a comprehensive catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems. It enables organizations to select controls based on the system's FIPS 199 impact level, ensuring a risk-based approach to safeguarding operations and assets.
intent: Establish a structured methodology for selecting and implementing security and privacy controls.
conditions: Applies to all federal systems and contractors supporting federal agencies under FISMA or RMF frameworks.
implementation_guidance: Identify system categorization via FIPS 199, then select a baseline of controls based on NIST SP 800-53 guidance. Tailor controls based on system needs and document them in the SSP. Implement selected controls and conduct assessments using guidance from NIST SP 800-53A.
assessment_method: Control-by-control testing and document review aligned to NIST SP 800-53A.
metadata: {"penalties":"Failure to implement required controls may result in denial or revocation of ATO, findings in audits, or breaches of contract terms.","reciprocity":"Forms the basis for RMF and is used across FedRAMP, FISMA, and DoD ATO processes.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Representation Regarding Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment
description: Requires contractors to disclose whether they use any covered telecommunications equipment or services produced by Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, or Dahua. This is a proactive disclosure requirement prior to contract award.
intent: Enable federal agencies to assess and avoid procurement of technologies posing supply chain risks.
conditions: Mandatory representation included in nearly all solicitations and contracts.
implementation_guidance: Conduct an internal assessment to identify any use of covered technologies. If such technologies are used, complete the representation with a full disclosure and mitigation plan. Coordinate with agency to determine acceptability prior to award.
assessment_method: Pre-award representations and post-award audits.
metadata: {"penalties":"False representation may trigger False Claims Act liability, contract suspension, or disqualification.","reciprocity":"Supports enforcement of Section 889 of the FY19 NDAA.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
description: This clause requires contractors to apply 15 basic safeguarding controls to protect Federal Contract Information (FCI) in nonfederal systems. It forms the minimum cybersecurity baseline for any federal contractor.
intent: Safeguard FCI on contractor-owned IT systems that are not intended to process classified information.
conditions: Applies to any contract where a contractor may store, process, or transmit FCI.
implementation_guidance: Implement basic protections such as access control, system monitoring, patching, and physical safeguards. Ensure policies are documented and systems are monitored for unauthorized access or usage.
assessment_method: Proposal representations and post-award compliance spot checks.
metadata: {"penalties":"Failure to implement required safeguards can lead to contractual remedies or termination for default.","reciprocity":"Serves as a foundation for DFARS 7012 and NIST 800-171 for CUI protection.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Cyber Incident Information
description: Protects incident data that contractors submit. It states that any information a contractor reports to DoD about a cyber incident (per DFARS 7012) shall not be used or released by the Government for purposes other than cybersecurity or law enforcement related to that incident. In effect, it ensures that sensitive info the contractor shares (e.g. network diagrams, vulnerabilities, proprietary info) won't be disclosed publicly or used to the contractor's detriment. Authorized persons (DoD cyber personnel) can use the info only to improve security or address the incident. This clause must be flowed down to subcontractors as well.
intent: Protect the confidentiality of cyber incident information and evidence shared with the DoD.
conditions: Applies when a cyber incident is reported under DFARS 252.204-7012.
implementation_guidance: When reporting an incident under DFARS 7012, mark the submission as containing "Contractor Proprietary Information – submitted under DFARS 252.204-7009" (DoD's DIBNet portal does much of this automatically). Contractors don't have to take action beyond normal incident reporting – this clause mainly binds the Government. Just be aware that the Government and any third parties it involves (e.g. DC3 or DIB CS program analysts) are required to protect your data. Flow this clause to subs so that they too have assurance their incident reports are protected and understand any incident info you share with them can't be misused.
assessment_method: Post-incident review by DoD or IG.
metadata: {"penalties":"There is no direct penalty on the contractor in this clause (it's protective of the contractor's info). For the Government, unauthorized use or release of a contractor's incident information could violate the contract and federal law – potentially leading to administrative or legal consequences for the individuals responsible. (For the contractor's benefit: this protection encourages candid reporting. If a contractor were to misuse another contractor's incident data, that could lead to liability as well.)","reciprocity":"Shared confidentiality obligations in incident handling.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Transition Planning for Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6)
description: OMB M-05-22 mandates that all federal agencies transition their network backbones to support IPv6, ensuring future interoperability and scalability. The policy promotes the use of IPv6 across all new IT acquisitions.
intent: Promote modernization of government networks and improve addressing capabilities.
conditions: Applies to all federal agency networks and contractors providing network infrastructure.
implementation_guidance: Ensure new IT systems support IPv6. Update network configurations and validate capability to transmit, receive, and process IPv6 traffic. Submit transition plans to OMB as required.
assessment_method: Technical network assessments and agency compliance reporting.
metadata: {"penalties":"Failure to transition may impact system interoperability or funding approvals.","reciprocity":"Supports broader IT modernization and cybersecurity posture goals.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems
description: NIST SP 800-171 outlines 110 security controls across 14 families specifically tailored for safeguarding Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in nonfederal systems, such as those owned by contractors. It derives its baseline from NIST SP 800-53, but is streamlined for non-governmental environments.
intent: Ensure that contractors adequately safeguard CUI outside federal facilities.
conditions: Applies to any contractor handling CUI under a federal contract, especially DoD contracts referencing DFARS 252.204-7012.
implementation_guidance: Review all 110 controls. Conduct a gap analysis. Create a System Security Plan (SSP) and a Plan of Actions and Milestones (POA&M). Implement all feasible controls, and document mitigations or timelines for any remaining gaps. Coordinate with DoD if required.
assessment_method: Self-assessment, or third-party assessment under CMMC or similar frameworks.
metadata: {"penalties":"Non-compliance can lead to contract termination, breach notifications, or False Claims Act exposure. Gaps must be addressed to maintain eligibility.","reciprocity":"Required for CMMC Level 2. Mapped to NIST 800-53 moderate controls.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Compliance with Safeguarding Controls (Solicitation Provision)
description: A pre-contract assurance: by submitting an offer, the offeror represents that it either will implement NIST SP 800-171 prior to contract start, or has notified the DoD CIO of any proposed exceptions ("variances") to 800-171. Essentially, this clause forces contractors at the bidding stage to affirm they meet (or will meet) the security requirements of DFARS 7012. If an offeror needs to deviate from any 800-171 control, they must explain why and get DoD CIO approval prior to award.
intent: Ensure contractors are aware of and prepared to comply with cyber safeguarding requirements before contract execution.
conditions: Included in solicitations where DFARS 252.204-7012 is expected to apply.
implementation_guidance: Before contract award, conduct a self-assessment against NIST SP 800-171. Document any gaps. If fully compliant, simply ensure you can say "We will/have implement(ed) all 110 controls." If not, prepare a written explanation for each unmet control with rationale or alternative safeguard (this is often called a "providing a SSP & POA&M" for the offer). Submit those to the Contracting Officer to be adjudicated by the DoD CIO. Await approval of any variances before contract award – if DoD rejects the variance, bring that control into compliance. Essentially, do not bid (or disclose gaps) if you cannot meet 800-171 requirements.
assessment_method: Proposal review by contracting officer.
metadata: {"penalties":"An offeror who cannot meet or does not commit to the 800-171 requirements may be found non-responsive or unawardable. Post-award, if a contractor was dishonest in representing compliance, it could lead to contract termination or False Claims Act exposure. Once the contract is in place, DFARS 7012 enforcement applies – failure to actually implement the controls can result in breach of contract. In short, non-compliance means no contract, or loss of one.","reciprocity":"Linked via DFARS safeguarding structure.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Basic and Enhanced Safeguarding of Contractor Information Systems
description: FAR 4.21 implements policies from OMB and NIST for securing contractor information systems that store, process, or transmit FCI. It covers both basic (FAR 52.204-21) and additional safeguarding measures when required.
intent: Provide a policy foundation for clause 52.204-21 and support enhanced controls where risk warrants.
conditions: Applies to any contractor handling FCI not designated as CUI or classified.
implementation_guidance: Adhere to baseline controls in FAR 52.204-21 and coordinate with agency-specific requirements for higher-risk systems. Track emerging threats and ensure cyber hygiene policies are maintained.
assessment_method: System audits, contract data reviews, and vendor attestations.
metadata: {"penalties":"Non-compliance may result in loss of contract opportunities or cybersecurity breach response liabilities.","reciprocity":"Serves as an umbrella policy tying to FISMA, NIST, and DFARS guidance.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: General Data Protection Regulation (EU)
description: The GDPR regulates the collection, use, and storage of personal data of individuals in the European Union. It imposes strict requirements on consent, data rights, security measures, and international data transfers.
intent: Protect the fundamental rights of individuals in the EU regarding their personal data.
conditions: Applies to any organization offering goods/services to or monitoring behavior of EU data subjects.
implementation_guidance: Implement data minimization, consent management, subject access processes, and breach response plans. Assign a Data Protection Officer (DPO) if required, and conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) where appropriate.
assessment_method: Supervisory authority audits and internal compliance assessments.
metadata: {"penalties":"Fines up to €20M or 4% of global turnover. Noncompliance may also result in bans on data processing.","reciprocity":"Some overlap with U.S. privacy laws (CCPA, CPRA) and NIST privacy frameworks.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules (Rev. 3)
description: FIPS 140-3 updates the FIPS 140-2 standard and aligns more closely with ISO/IEC 19790:2012. It outlines security requirements for cryptographic modules, enabling stronger conformance to modern practices and testing methods.
intent: Modernize and enhance federal cryptographic validation standards.
conditions: Applies to new cryptographic implementations and procurement after May 2022 or as directed by agencies.
implementation_guidance: Follow updated FIPS 140-3 validation processes and reference the Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP). New procurements should prefer FIPS 140-3 validated modules unless legacy exceptions are approved.
assessment_method: CMVP certification review and acquisition checks.
metadata: {"penalties":"Non-compliance may result in rejection of products or system reauthorization delays.","reciprocity":"Required by NIST, FedRAMP, and DoD cybersecurity programs for cryptographic compliance.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Managing Information as a Strategic Resource (Privacy Provisions)
description: OMB Circular A-130 establishes general policy for the planning, collection, use, and dissemination of federal information resources. It requires agencies to implement privacy programs to protect personally identifiable information (PII).
intent: Ensure the privacy and security of PII managed by federal agencies and contractors.
conditions: Applies to all federal agencies and contractors handling or accessing federal PII.
implementation_guidance: Develop and maintain privacy impact assessments (PIAs), system of records notices (SORNs), and privacy training programs. Establish safeguards for electronic records and breach response procedures.
assessment_method: Review of privacy documentation and compliance audits.
metadata: {"penalties":"Non-compliance may result in privacy breaches, legal liability, and loss of contract eligibility.","reciprocity":"Integrated into NIST 800-53 (privacy controls) and FISMA compliance programs.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: California Consumer Privacy Act
description: The CCPA grants California residents rights over their personal data, including the right to know, delete, and opt-out of the sale of their data. It applies to for-profit entities meeting certain revenue or data-processing thresholds.
intent: Provide transparency and control to California consumers over their personal information.
conditions: Applies to businesses operating in California that meet thresholds related to revenue or data volume.
implementation_guidance: Publish privacy notices, enable opt-out mechanisms, and respond to consumer data requests within statutory timelines. Implement reasonable security measures and train employees on data handling practices.
assessment_method: Attorney General enforcement actions and internal policy reviews.
metadata: {"penalties":"Civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation or $7,500 for intentional violations.","reciprocity":"Predecessor to CPRA. Shares conceptual overlap with GDPR and some NIST controls.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Implementation of Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12 (HSPD-12)
description: OMB M-05-24 provides implementation guidance for HSPD-12, directing agencies to adopt a government-wide standard for secure identity verification via PIV credentials.
intent: Standardize identity credentials for federal employees and contractors.
conditions: Applies to all agencies and contractors accessing federal facilities or information systems.
implementation_guidance: Issue PIV credentials per FIPS 201. Ensure physical and logical access systems are compatible with PIV cards. Coordinate with agency security officers for implementation milestones.
assessment_method: Credential audits and access system inspections.
metadata: {"penalties":"Lack of PIV support may restrict personnel access and system authorization.","reciprocity":"Implements and enforces HSPD-12 standards across federal agencies.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: DoD Access to Information Systems for Cyber Assessment
description: Allows the DoD to audit the contractor's 800-171 implementation. If included, the contractor agrees to provide DoD (specifically, the DoD CIO or designee) access to its facilities, systems, and personnel as needed to perform a Higher-Level DoD Assessment of compliance. In practice, if DoD is concerned about a contractor's SPRS self-score, they can conduct a thorough review (e.g. request documentation, interviews, or even verify technical controls). DoD will give the contractor an advance notice. The clause is essentially DoD's right-to-audit for cybersecurity.
intent: Enable DoD to independently verify the implementation of required security controls.
conditions: Mandatory when DFARS 252.204-7019 is invoked.
implementation_guidance: Be prepared for a Government audit of your cybersecurity program. Maintain documentation of your NIST 800-171 control implementation (System Security Plan, network diagrams, policies, etc.) and your POA&M for pending items. When notified of a DoD assessment, promptly provide requested evidence or on-site access to company IT staff and systems. Ensure key security personnel (CISO, IT admins) are available to answer questions. The DoD assessment team will assign a confidence level to your SPRS score or issue a new score. Cooperate fully to demonstrate good faith.
assessment_method: On-site or virtual audit by DoD assessors.
metadata: {"penalties":"If you refuse to accommodate an authorized DoD assessment, it will likely be considered a breach of contract, risking termination or other remedy. A poor result in the DoD-conducted assessment (revealing major non-implementation of controls) can lead to corrective action requirements or affect your ability to get future contracts until issues are fixed. In extreme cases, it could trigger contract termination for default if the lack of security is deemed a serious failure.","reciprocity":"Aligned with CMMC verification access.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules
description: FIPS 140-2 specifies security requirements for cryptographic modules used within federal information systems. It defines four increasing levels of security (Levels 1–4), covering physical security, key management, and module authentication.
intent: Ensure standardized and validated encryption is used to protect sensitive federal data.
conditions: Applies to any federal system or contractor that uses encryption to protect sensitive but unclassified (SBU) information.
implementation_guidance: Only use cryptographic modules that have been validated under the FIPS 140-2 program by NIST. Maintain proof of validation. Reference applicable modules in the System Security Plan (SSP).
assessment_method: Validation review of encryption modules used in systems.
metadata: {"penalties":"Use of non-validated encryption can result in audit findings, loss of ATO, or breach of data security requirements.","reciprocity":"Mandatory for FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, DFARS 7012, and CMMC cryptographic controls.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC)
description: Requires contractors to achieve a Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification at a specified level (Level 1 (Foundational), Level 2 (Advanced), or Level 3 (Expert), depending on contract) as a condition of contract award. CMMC is DoD's program of third-party cybersecurity certification: Level 1 roughly equals basic FAR 52.204-21 practices, Level 2 aligns with NIST SP 800-171 (110 controls) for protecting CUI, and Level 3 (to be defined, likely adds NIST SP 800-172 enhanced controls for critical programs). DFARS 7021, when invoked, says the contractor shall maintain the required CMMC certification (by an accredited CMMC auditor) throughout the performance of the contract. It must also ensure subcontractors have the appropriate CMMC level prior to handling info. Status: CMMC 2.0 (with 3 levels) is being rolled out; DFARS 7021 is expected to be updated in 2024/2025 to match the new model and made a contract requirement following rulemaking.
intent: Standardize and verify cybersecurity readiness across the defense industrial base.
conditions: Required based on contract-specific sensitivity or program designation.
implementation_guidance: m
assessment_method: Third-party assessment (C3PAO) or Self-Attestation
metadata: {"penalties":"An offeror without the required CMMC certificate will not be eligible for award of new DoD contracts that include this clause. If a certification lapses or is revoked during contract performance, the contractor could be found in breach; DoD may suspend work or terminate the contract. False claims about certification status or control implementation can lead to severe legal penalties (False Claims Act). In addition, CMMC will likely become a gatekeeper – companies without it will lose DoD business opportunities entirely.","reciprocity":"NIST 800-171","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of PII
description: OMB M-17-12 establishes requirements for federal agencies to prepare for and respond to breaches involving PII. It sets thresholds for reporting, mitigation, and communication with affected individuals.
intent: Minimize the impact of privacy incidents and improve breach response readiness.
conditions: Applies to agencies and contractors with access to or responsibility for federal PII.
implementation_guidance: Develop incident response plans specific to PII breaches. Train personnel on breach response protocols. Coordinate breach assessments with agency privacy officers and follow reporting timelines.
assessment_method: Incident response plan reviews and breach response performance audits.
metadata: {"penalties":"Improper handling of a breach may lead to legal exposure, audit findings, and reputational damage.","reciprocity":"Mapped to NIST 800-53 IR and AR control families and supports privacy compliance.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
description: An interim requirement pending CMMC full rollout: it requires contractors to have a current (<=3 years old) NIST 800-171 self-assessment on record in the DoD Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) database prior to contract award. The contractor must score their implementation of 800-171 (out of 110) using DoD's scoring methodology and post that score. If using subcontractors that handle CUI, the prime contractor must ensure those subKs have an assessment score posted as well. The clause essentially formalizes that DoD will verify compliance status via SPRS.
intent: Ensure transparency and maturity of contractor cybersecurity posture.
conditions: Required when DFARS 252.204-7012 is included in a contract.
implementation_guidance: Conduct a Basic self-assessment per DoD's Assessment Methodology (each unmet 800-171 requirement subtracts points from 110). Post your score (and basic info like assessment date and system covered) to the SPRS website. If your score is less than 110 (i.e. not all controls implemented), develop a Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) to address the gaps – you may need to provide this to the contracting officer. Ensure each subcontractor that will handle CUI also does the SPRS self-assessment and provides you their score attestation (the clause prevents awarding subcontracts to those without a current assessment). Maintain/upkeep this score – ideally improving it over time until reaching 110.
assessment_method: Self-assessment or DoD-conducted review.
metadata: {"penalties":"DoD will not award new contracts (or options) if the contractor does not have a current assessment in SPRS – you could be ineligible for selection. A false or misleading self-assessment (e.g. overestimating compliance) could be considered a false statement to the Government, with potential False Claims Act or suspension/debarment consequences. Once under contract, if DoD requests a higher-level assessment (e.g. a Medium or High assessment by DoD officials), you must comply or risk contract default. Additionally, a persistently low score without improvement plans may affect past performance or lead to additional oversight by DoD (including possible on-site audits under DFARS 7020).","reciprocity":"Supports CMMC and DFARS compliance validation.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Enabling Mission Delivery through Improved Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM)
description: OMB M-19-17 establishes ICAM policy for the federal government. It mandates agency-wide implementation of standards and governance for managing digital identities, credentials, and logical access to systems.
intent: Strengthen federal digital identity infrastructure and streamline access control.
conditions: Applies to all executive branch agencies and contractors supporting identity or access services.
implementation_guidance: Implement ICAM programs aligned with NIST SP 800-63. Develop identity governance frameworks, enforce MFA, and monitor user lifecycle. Update enterprise architectures to support identity federation and attribute-based access control.
assessment_method: Identity system reviews, maturity models, and FISMA reporting.
metadata: {"penalties":"Delays in adoption may result in security vulnerabilities or OMB compliance risk.","reciprocity":"Directly referenced in NIST and FICAM programs and impacts NIST 800-53 IA controls.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Prohibition on Contracting for Hardware, Software, and Services Developed or Provided by Kaspersky Lab
description: Prohibits the use or procurement of hardware, software, or services developed or provided by Kaspersky Lab or any of its related entities. This clause addresses national security risks posed by foreign technology providers.
intent: Prevent federal systems from exposure to cybersecurity risks tied to Kaspersky Lab software and services.
conditions: Included in all solicitations and contracts, including those below the micro-purchase threshold.
implementation_guidance: Review IT asset inventory and vendor lists to ensure no components from Kaspersky Lab are in use. If found, immediately remove and notify the contracting officer. Update procurement controls to block future acquisitions.
assessment_method: Vendor inventory reviews and contract compliance reporting.
metadata: {"penalties":"Use of prohibited technologies may result in contract termination, loss of eligibility, or cybersecurity incident response.","reciprocity":"Aligns with supply chain risk directives and Section 1634 of the FY18 NDAA.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12
description: HSPD-12 mandates a government-wide standard for secure and reliable forms of identification for federal employees and contractors. It led to the development of the PIV (Personal Identity Verification) credentialing system.
intent: Ensure consistent and secure access control across federal facilities and systems.
conditions: Applies to all federal agencies and contractors requiring physical or logical access to government systems.
implementation_guidance: Implement PIV credential issuance and validation systems in accordance with NIST SP 800-116 and FIPS 201. Ensure systems recognize and enforce PIV-based authentication.
assessment_method: Access control audits and credential validation checks.
metadata: {"penalties":"Failure to comply may restrict access to federal systems and limit contract eligibility.","reciprocity":"Required under FISMA, OMB A-130, and NIST 800-53 control IA-2.","last_updated":"2025-05-18"}

title: California Privacy Rights Act
description: The CPRA amends and expands the CCPA, introducing new rights (e.g., correction, restriction), more detailed data processing rules, and the establishment of the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) to enforce the law.
intent: Strengthen California's consumer privacy framework and align more closely with GDPR-like protections.
conditions: Applies to covered entities under CCPA and extends requirements to sensitive personal information.
implementation_guidance: Update privacy policies, enable new consumer rights (correction, restriction), and maintain data retention limits. Implement risk assessments for sensitive data and cooperate with CPPA investigations.
assessment_method: CPPA regulatory reviews and internal privacy program evaluations.
